proof:
# Simultaneous convex partition realization of all feasible base moments

Let C be a compact convex body in R^n x R^d. Let its mixed intersection
have intrinsic dimension q>=1, and write mu=H_q|S. Let P index its positive
q-volume fibers K_z, with weights w_z and vectors v_z=(1,z).

Fix k>=1 labeled classes and feasible class moment vectors

    r_i=(t_i,m_i), i=1,...,k,

meaning there are numbers s_(i,z)>=0 with

    sum_i s_(i,z)=w_z,
    r_i=sum_z s_(i,z)v_z.                              (1)

Discard classes of mass t_i=0. Then there exist convex bodies
`D_1,...,D_k`, each obtained by intersecting C with at most k-1 closed
ambient halfspaces, such that:

    union_i D_i=C,
    mu(D_i intersect D_j)=0 for i!=j,
    (mu(D_i), integral_(D_i) z dmu)=r_i.               (2)

In particular all mass is exhausted exactly. If m_i=t_i j_i with integer
j_i, the TRUE unweighted intrinsic centroid of `D_i intersect Lambda`
has base j_i and belongs to that mixed set.

The partition can be prescribed to use continuous score vectors u_i
whose pairwise differences are nonconstant on every positive fiber.
Such vectors always exist: choose one generic continuous vector u,
nonconstant on all positive fiber direction spaces, and set u_i=i u.
The theorem does NOT assert that these cells can be extracted one at a
time by single hyperplane cuts while keeping the remaining set convex.
It is an actual simultaneous convex polyhedral partition.

## 1. The exact feasible moment polytope

Let e_i be the coordinate vectors of R^k and view the k-tuple of class
moments in V=(R^(n+1))^k. The feasible polytope is

    Z=sum_z w_z conv{e_i tensor v_z:i=1,...,k}.         (3)

This is exactly (1), because each fiber distributes its mass among the
classes with nonnegative proportions. Put U=span(Z-Z), the direction
space of its affine hull.

For theta=(theta_1,...,theta_k) in V define

    Psi(theta)=sum_z integral_(K_z)
                  max_i(theta_i.v_z+u_i.x) dH_q(x).

The maximum is unique almost everywhere on every positive fiber:
any tie lies in a proper intrinsic hyperplane, by the condition on
u_i-u_j. Consequently Psi is continuously differentiable, and its
ith gradient block is

    (gradient Psi(theta))_i
      =sum_z v_z H_q{ x in K_z:
          theta_i.v_z+u_i.x >= theta_j.v_z+u_j.x for all j }.  (4)

Difference quotients are uniformly bounded by fixed coordinates of v_z;
pointwise convergence outside the finite union of tie hyperplanes proves
(4) and continuity by dominated convergence. The gradient belongs to Z.

The support function of (3) is

    h_Z(theta)=sum_z w_z max_i(theta_i.v_z).

Since changing every entry of a finite maximum by at most B changes its
value by at most B,

    |Psi(theta)-h_Z(theta)|
      <=sum_z integral_(K_z) max_i |u_i.x| dH_q(x)=A<infinity.  (5)

## 2. Relative-interior targets, including all affine gauges

Suppose r=(r_1,...,r_k) belongs to relint Z. There is epsilon>0 with
`r+epsilon B_U subset Z`. Thus for theta in U,

    h_Z(theta)-theta.r>=epsilon|theta|.

By (5), `Psi(theta)-theta.r` is coercive on U and has a minimizer there.
Its restricted gradient vanishes. Since both gradient Psi and r belong
to Z, their difference belongs to U; the restricted vanishing is
therefore the full equality `gradient Psi=r`.

This handles all common-score gauges and all dependencies among the base
coordinates. No full-dimensionality of Z in V or unjustified strict
convexity of Psi is required.

## 3. Boundary targets and allowed class sets

For r on the relative boundary, let F be its minimal face in Z. Choose
an exposing vector omega=(omega_1,...,omega_k) with

    F={zeta in Z:omega.zeta=h_Z(omega)},   r in relint F.

Such a vector exists for every polytope face: add positive multiples of
the finitely many facet normals whose equalities define the face.
For each source index z let

    I_z={i:omega_i.v_z=max_j omega_j.v_z}.

The Minkowski-sum face formula gives exactly

    F=sum_z w_z conv{e_i tensor v_z:i in I_z}.         (6)

Thus this face permits only the labels I_z in each summand of (3).

Repeat Sections 1--2 with the maximum restricted to `i in I_z` in each
fiber, the polytope F in place of Z, and direction space `span(F-F)`.
The same null-tie proof, bounded-error estimate, and relative-interior
coercivity give a finite vector theta_0 whose restricted winner moments
are exactly r. If F is a singleton the gradient necessarily equals that
point, and the zero-dimensional minimization is immediate.

Set theta=theta_0+T omega. On each fiber, all allowed labels acquire the same
added score. Every disallowed label has a strictly smaller coefficient
of T. There are finitely many fibers and labels, and all the continuous
scores are bounded on their compact fibers. Thus one sufficiently large
FINITE T makes every disallowed label strictly lose throughout that
fiber. The allowed winners are unchanged. Hence the unrestricted
potential at theta also has gradient exactly r.

The argument realizes boundary targets exactly; it does not pass to an
infinite score limit or lose mass on supporting fibers.

## 4. Actual convex cells, exhaustive coverage, and centers

Define the affine scores on the full ambient space by

    L_i(z,x)=theta_i.(1,z)+u_i.x,

and let

    D_i=C intersect {L_i>=L_j for every j}.

These compact convex sets cover C because a finite maximum is always
attained. Their pairwise intersections lie in score-tie hyperplanes,
which have zero mu measure. Equation (4) proves their exact mass and
base moments. Every retained t_i is positive, so some point of C belongs
strictly to its winner cell: the finite union of tie hyperplanes has
zero mu measure. Interior points of C approximate that point and retain
all its strict score inequalities. Thus D_i has nonempty ambient interior
and is a convex body. Its mixed intrinsic dimension remains q.

Its true intrinsic barycenter belongs to D_i by convexity. When its base
moment is t_i j_i with integer j_i, it therefore belongs to
`D_i intersect Lambda`. This proves all of (2), including exact center
membership and exhaustion of the original mass.

## 5. Scope

Only positive intrinsic dimension supplies the null-tie property. Pure
counting atoms cannot generally be split into arbitrary feasible fractional
class moments, so no q=0 purification claim is made. This theorem concerns
mass/base moments of uniform measures on ACTUAL convex pieces, not merely
fractional source densities. It nevertheless gives no halfspace-depth
constant at their centroids and no OC conclusion by itself.

## 6. An exact partition into at most 2^n integer-centroid convex bodies

Combine this theorem with `candidate 7e12497595d939f1`.
For clarity, its finite merging argument is recalled here. Positive
q-volume bases P are lattice-convex by the dimension of Minkowski averages.
Choose a nonnegative array c_(j,z), indexed by P twice, satisfying

    sum_j c_(j,z)=w_z,
    sum_z (z-j)c_(j,z)=0,

and minimizing `sum_j |j|^2 sum_z c_(j,z)`. The diagonal array is feasible,
and this is a compact finite linear program. At a minimizer, let V be the
positive target indices. If distinct targets j_i have an integer convex
combination j with positive coefficients lambda_i, remove a sufficiently
small mass epsilon lambda_i from each row, proportionally across its
sources, and add all the removed mass to row j. Lattice convexity puts j
in P. Every column total and every target barycenter remain correct, while
the objective decreases by

    epsilon sum_i lambda_i |j_i-j|^2>0.

This is impossible. Thus V is the vertex set of its convex hull, that hull
has no other lattice points, and no two elements of V share parity.
In particular `|V|<=2^n`.

Apply the simultaneous realization theorem using ONLY the labels in V and
their positive target mass/base moments. The resulting actual convex bodies
D_j satisfy

    union_(j in V) D_j=C,
    H_q((D_i intersect D_j) intersect Lambda)=0 for i!=j,
    sum_(j in V) H_q(D_j intersect Lambda)=H_q(S),

and each true intrinsic centroid has integer base j and belongs to its own
mixed piece. Every label has positive mass, so there are NO additional
zero-mass cells to remove: the displayed union is literally all of C.
Lower-dimensional original fibers may occur on cell boundaries, but carry
zero H_q mass and do not change these assertions.

The number 2^n is sharp. For `C=[0,1]^n x K` with K full dimensional,
every positive class with integer base centroid is supported on one binary
base vertex, because each mean coordinate is either zero or one. All 2^n
positive fibers must be assigned, so at least 2^n positive classes are
necessary, even for a fractional partition. Conversely the construction
above uses at most that many actual convex pieces.

This is an exhaustive convex partition theorem with controlled count. It
does not assert a recursive sequence of single halfspace cuts, and it does
not assign continuous Grünbaum depth to the mixed centroids of its pieces.
